name: Probe legs: pass probe_cmd through a file so quotes survive PowerShell 5.1, and a silent green probe is not a pass
note: FIRST: in your worktree run `git merge --no-edit worktree-wf_42f40752-0fd-1` (the BP9-NONETIER branch, commit 5a2779f2, verdict SOUND-WITH-NITS) and read harness/notes/bp9/wave2_results.json entry BP9-NONETIER for the crucible's findings. Two fixes. (1) harness/orchestrate.ps1 near line 512 passes `--cmd $leg.probe_cmd` to python under Windows PowerShell 5.1, which re-tokenises embedded double quotes, so a probe like `python -c "print('ACCEPT: x :: pass :: ok')"` dies with 'unrecognized arguments' and the fallback writes a `missing` receipt that misreports the cause as 'row carries no probe_cmd'. Fix: compile_wave.py writes the probe command to a file beside the prompt (prompts/<ID>.probe.cmd, UTF-8, verbatim) and the row carries probe_cmd_file; probe_receipt.py gains `run --cmd-file <path>` (reads the command verbatim, no shell re-tokenising on the way in); the ps1 passes --cmd-file; when the runner exits non-zero without writing a receipt, the ps1 writes a distinct 'runner failed' receipt whose finding carries the runner's stderr head, not the 'no probe_cmd' text. (2) probe_receipt.py: a probe that exits 0 but prints zero ACCEPT lines must yield status fail with a finding 'probe printed no ACCEPT lines' (a silent green is not a pass; SCREEN treats empty acceptance as a non-verdict). Extend tests/test_rails_none_tier.py: a quoted command round-trips through --cmd-file and yields the ACCEPT row; exit 0 with no ACCEPT lines is status fail; the ps1 static test asserts --cmd-file is what the launch line passes.
